solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Arranged priests to take saucy examination

indicators.note: things arranged are put in a new order, so the letters of the clue word are reshuffled

parts.note: arch means cheeky or saucy, as in an arch look

explanation.surface: Some clergymen are cast in a racy scene involving a cheeky inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranged' turns PRIESTS into STRIPSE; 'to take' simply links it to ARCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A full body search of someone with clothes removed is a type of examination, usually by police or customs.

clue.text: Conceal confidential note

parts.note: something confidential is secret
E is one of the musical notes A to G

explanation.surface: Hide a private memo.
explanation.definitionFit: To secrete something is to hide it away, a verb synonym of conceal.

clue.text: Disturb with sound arguments

indicators.note: sound here tells us the answer is a word heard like another, not its spelling

parts.note: rows are quarrels or arguments

explanation.surface: Unsettle someone by reasoning soundly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound arguments' reads as valid reasoning, but 'sound' is the homophone signal and ROWS (rhyming with cows) is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse is to wake or stir up, a synonym of disturb.

clue.text: Poet excited with fruit cake

indicators.note: excited letters are agitated and stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A bard gets worked up over a fruity dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges POET and FRUIT together; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A petit four is a small fancy cake or biscuit served after a meal.

clue.text: Some conversed in Gaelic

indicators.note: some of the word means only part of its letters are taken

explanation.surface: Some people chatted in a Celtic tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes a run of letters from inside 'conversed'; 'in' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for the Gaelic language of Scotland or Ireland.

clue.text: Fell Race entrant who didn't win?

definitions.text: Fell Race entrant who didn't win?

parts.words: Fell Race entrant who didn't win?
parts.note: a competitor in a hill race who finished second rather than first; 'fell' also hints the runner went down

explanation.surface: A hill-running competitor who failed to take first place.
explanation.walkthrough: A fell race is a British cross-country race over hills and moorland; the answer is the competitor who came second.
explanation.definitionFit: The one finishing second in a contest is the person placed just behind the winner.

clue.text: Poor house for student near Brighton

indicators.note: near says the second piece sits right beside the first, following it

parts.note: Hove is the town adjoining Brighton on the English south coast
L is the learner plate sign, used for a student

explanation.surface: Cheap lodgings for a young scholar on the Sussex coast.
explanation.walkthrough: HOVE is a seaside town joined to Brighton (the two form one city); 'for' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A hovel is a squalid, wretched dwelling, a poor house.

clue.text: Pops round to unload guilt

parts.note: to drop something is to let it go or unload it
sin is wrongdoing, the cause of guilt

explanation.surface: A visitor calls by to confess and ease the conscience.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop in is to pay a casual visit, the same idiom as pop round.

clue.text: Influence of converted priest, say, is mounting

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged
in a down clue, mounting means climbing up, so the piece reads bottom to top

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: A newly converted cleric's clout is growing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' makes PRESTI from PRIEST; 'mounting' turns EG into GE; 'is' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Prestige is standing or reputation that gives sway, a synonym of influence.

clue.text: No curates should take her out

definitions.text: No curates should take her out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown out of order and remade

explanation.surface: Clergy are warned not to date a woman of easy virtue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges NO CURATES; the whole clue also describes a woman the clergy should avoid escorting.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtesan is a high-class kept woman, someone a curate should not escort.

clue.text: Sign of resistance in Spanish port

indicators.note: in places the resistance letter inside the port's name

parts.note: Vigo is a port in Galicia, Spain
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A token of defiance shown in a harbour in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgo is one of the twelve zodiac signs, the Virgin.

clue.text: Passes out at college

parts.note: permits allowing students to leave a school or college for a time, not graduating

explanation.surface: Students graduate from university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passes out' suggests graduating, but these are leave passes: Latin for 'let him go out'.
explanation.definitionFit: These are formal permissions granted in British schools and colleges for temporary absence.

clue.text: They won't stand for their instruments being played

definitions.text: They won't stand for their instruments being played

parts.words: They won't stand for their instruments being played
parts.note: reads as people objecting to their instruments being used, but means musicians who sit down to play

explanation.surface: Owners object to others using their instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'won't stand for' suggests intolerance; literally these players must be seated to play a large bowed instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Players of the large stringed instrument held between the knees always perform sitting.

clue.text: Inventor having no team backing

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the pieces read from the end

parts.note: taken as written
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: An inventor working without the support of a crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses NO SIDE as one run; 'having' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was the American inventor of the phonograph and a practical light bulb.

clue.text: The little devil! Telling stories and making insinuations

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous devil
telling stories is a euphemism for lying

explanation.surface: Scolding a mischievous child who fibs and hints at things.
explanation.definitionFit: Implying means suggesting indirectly, which is what insinuating does.

clue.text: Official ceremony that means work

definitions.meaning: a formal social event or reception
to operate or perform as intended

explanation.surface: A formal event that counts as a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A function is a formal gathering, and to function is to work or operate.

clue.text: Implicated — and worried?

definitions.meaning: involved or having a part in something

explanation.surface: Involved and anxious about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Concerned means both involved in a matter and anxious about something.

clue.text: Left in rush, but made statement

indicators.note: in puts the side word inside the plant word

parts.note: a rush is a reed-like marsh plant
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone left in a hurry but gave an account first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rush' looks like haste, but it is the waterside plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Reported means gave an account or made a statement about something.

clue.text: I am getting stout as a businessman

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
porter is a dark beer like stout

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of putting on weight like a well-fed merchant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stout' looks like fat, but it is the dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: An importer is a trader who brings goods in from abroad, a kind of businessman.

clue.text: A sailor can't be far out with such navigation

definitions.text: A sailor can't be far out with such navigation

parts.words: A sailor can't be far out with such navigation
parts.note: reads as navigation too accurate to be in error, but means sailing kept close to the coast

explanation.surface: Navigation so precise a sailor could not be badly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'far out' suggests a large error; literally the boat stays near the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Inshore navigation keeps close to land rather than going out to open sea.

clue.text: Popular with nurse, so propose!

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
to tend is to look after or nurse

explanation.surface: A man in favour with a nurse decides to pop the question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'propose' suggests marriage, but means plan.
explanation.definitionFit: To intend is to plan or propose to do something.

clue.text: Power line that may last for many years

definitions.text: Power line that may last for many years

parts.words: Power line that may last for many years
parts.note: reads as a durable electricity cable, but means a succession of ruling family members

explanation.surface: An electricity cable built to endure for decades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power line' suggests electricity; here it is a line of descent holding power.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynasty is a succession of rulers from one family, holding power across generations.

clue.text: Rev up?

parts.note: reads as making an engine roar, but means a reverend who is up in the air flying

explanation.surface: Gun the engine.
explanation.walkthrough: Rev is short for Reverend; the answer is slang for a clergyman, especially a forces chaplain.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a clergyman or chaplain, imagined here as a parson flying up aloft.

clue.text: One can't imagine being without them

definitions.text: One can't imagine being without them

parts.words: One can't imagine being without them
parts.note: reads as something indispensable, but literally imagining requires having notions

explanation.surface: Something so essential life without it is unthinkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can't imagine being without' sounds like devotion; literally, without notions you cannot imagine.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoughts or notions are what any act of imagination needs to work with.

clue.text: Horse on hire, having been broken

indicators.note: broken letters are smashed and put back in another order

explanation.surface: A rental horse that has been trained to the saddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' suggests breaking in a horse, but it rearranges ON HIRE; 'Horse' is slang for the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse is long-standing street slang for the drug diamorphine.

clue.text: Looked to go up, then went ahead

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the piece reads from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
led means went in front or ahead

explanation.surface: Someone eyed the climb, then set off in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns GO into OG; 'to' and 'then' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogled means stared at, often lecherously, a kind of looking.

clue.text: Weekend I've arranged in Russian city

parts.note: the end of the word week is its last letter

indicators.note: arranged letters are set out in a different order

explanation.surface: A weekend break planned in a city of the old Soviet Union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges I'VE to IEV; 'in' links. The city, now spelt Kyiv, is Ukraine's capital, called Russian in older usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiev was a major city of the Russian empire and Soviet Union, now Ukraine's capital.

clue.text: Tell everyone Ann lost weight

indicators.note: lost means the named woman is taken away from the longer word

parts.note: to announce is to tell everyone publicly
taken as written

explanation.surface: Broadcast the news that Ann has slimmed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost weight' suggests dieting; 'lost' removes ANN from ANNOUNCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ounce is a small imperial unit of weight, one sixteenth of a pound.

clue.text: What figures neat girls may display

indicators.note: may display suggests the letters can be laid out to show another word

explanation.surface: Asking what shapely bodies tidy young women show off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figures' reads as body shapes, but is geometric; 'What' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Three-sided plane shapes are among the basic figures of geometry.

clue.text: Time of year when the daffodils come out

definitions.text: Time of year when the daffodils come out

parts.words: Time of year when the daffodils come out
parts.note: reads as spring in general, but means the day the Welsh pin on their national flower

explanation.surface: The season when spring flowers bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: The daffodil is a national emblem of Wales, worn on the feast of its patron saint, 1 March.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh national day, 1 March, when people wear the daffodil emblem.
